author: Thomalon
title: False Advertising
content:
There is an advertisement with a female voiceover that states you will be guaranteed a $100 dollar in-game pack if you download the app directly through clicking on that ad. I downloaded it and got nothing; this is a lie. Thus, I promptly deleted it.

Aside from this, the ads for this game are outdated and clearly reuse models - such as the water bucket generator piece - from the developer’s other game, Gossip Harbor.

Back when I did have this game downloaded it had extremely manipulative tactics. You would get a streak of manufactured good luck for a few minutes, then it would run out and you would be enticed to spend gems or money on more energy. When you visit the game after not playing for a while it says “welcome back, we missed you” to breed a false sense of companionship and guilt-trip the player into continuing to play. 

In general the game has really bad balancing, with disproportionate chances for getting the second or third item from generators, especially when you need them the most. If you do still want to buy the game - because it does lack mandatory ads, as stated (though you can still watch some to earn rewards) - just don’t spend any money on it. Once I did, I lost the ability to watch an ad to get a full bar’s worth of energy from the energy boxes and chests. It was definitely fun for a while, especially in the start. Refreshing. The mechanic of having newer and newer generators was fun. But they reuse art from other games, utilize manipulative tactics to get the player to keep returning, and reuse art in events instead of drawing brand new art. For a game that is four years old by now, this kind of conduct is unacceptable; why even have ads if you won’t put in the effort of creating or commissioning someone to create original icons?

TL;DR: Bad game. It was fun at the start, but then it all dried out and greed ruined the experience.

author: Tiamat42
title: Pros and cons by a real person not a bot 🙄
content:
Pretty standard merge gameplay cut from the same unity-engine template most of them use. The art is generic and probably AI generated, but the story is slightly unique, if a bit hard to follow because conversations are tied to buildings so you just jump around between them as you renovate.

Gameplay is fine as long as you ignore the five or six events, races, points systems, etc thrown in your face at once. After a few days you can spend a full 100 energy bar on one generator and not get close to finishing one order. So racking up points or tokens for finishing lots of orders in a short time is impossible unless you’re also racking up that credit card bill. There’s also no ads to watch for extra energy or whatever, which is good and bad depending on how you feel about that, so it’s spend gems or wait.

If you can ignore all the FOMO and visual clutter and just play the story at your own pace, it’s fun.

title: Probability isn’t high enough.
content: Although this game is great because there are no ads involved and it has constant changing events being placed, I will say that the probability of receiving an item that you need once you get far into the game, is very small. I can tap on something to produce a specific item that would be considered “rare” to fulfill my order requests and it could take me days to create that order. I go through 300 energy a day just to get maybe 1-2 of ANOTHER item that I have to tap to create the item I actually need. I haven’t been this invested in a game before so it’s quite embarrassing to say I’ve spent money on it but it IS enjoyable once you fulfill them. Not to mention, you get to a point where you have over 1 milllion coins and nothing to do with them because you need to create wayyyy too many tools in order to build stuff and level up. Also, the events are quite impossible to complete if you are not spending money or playing every single time your energy gets filled up. Maybe that’s the point they want to get across but I’m starting to find that I’m receiving less and less of what I actually need to progress in the game.
